events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by an upstream dam release is expected. * WHERE...Central Yuma County in southwestern Arizona... * WHEN...Until 315 PM MST Friday Nov 27. * IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations is expected. events.title: Coastal Flood Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 2.0 ft of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding with up to 2.8 feet of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking waves of 20 to 30 feet. * WHERE...San Francisco County. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM PST Monday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 6 AM Monday to 4 PM PST Thursday. For the High Surf Warning, from midnight Tuesday night to midnight PST Wednesday night. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, numerous road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of drowning. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide is expected to be 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW) at 9:25 AM Monday, 2.6 ft above normal (8.4 ft MLLW) at 10:05 AM Tuesday, 2.8 ft above normal (8.6 ft MLLW) at 10:49 AM Wednesday, and 2.4 ft above normal (8.2 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.6 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

events.title: Coastal Flood Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, higher than normal astronomical tides (King Tides) are expected to bring up to 2.4 ft of inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways on Monday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, higher than normal astronomical tides (King Tides) combined with storm surge from large surf are expected to bring up to 3.1 ft of inundation above ground level Tuesday and Wednesday, with up to 2.6 ft of inundation expected on Thursday. * WHERE...Beaches and low lying areas along the shore lines of Douglas, Coos and Curry Counties. This includes the communities of North Bend, Charleston, Port Orford, Gold Beach, and Coos Bay. Coastal flooding is expected to impact portions of Highway 101 around Gold Beach, Coos Bay, and Reedsport. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 7 AM to 4 PM PST Monday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 7 AM Tuesday to 7 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. This event is expected see similar impacts to what occurred on January 3rd, 2026. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The worst conditions are expected to be during the high tide periods in the late morning/early afternoon. This is especially so for Tuesday and Wednesday as storm activity brings large breaking surf heights of 23 to 28 ft and adds storm surge to the water levels. Storm activity lessens on Thursday, but King Tides will still be present, which will likely continue inundation impacts. At the Charleston, OR tide gauge, high tide is expected to be at 10:09 AM Monday, at 10:51 AM Tuesday, at 11:35 AM Wednesday, and at 12:23 PM Thursday.

events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Watch, High astronomical tides and large surf with storm surge may cause moderate flooding in low lying areas along the Redwood/Mendocino Coast. Up to one foot of saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in low lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties. * WHEN...From Tuesday morning through Thursday afternoon during periods of high tide. * IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Some shoreline erosion may occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Expect continued increases in high tide water levels through the coming work week with the tide peaking on Wednesday. Prepare now and pay attention to official guidance on shelters and or resources available to the public.

For the Coastal Flood Warning, higher than normal astronomical tides (King Tides) combined with storm surge from large surf (breaking wave heights of 23 to 28 ft) are expected to bring up to 3.3 ft of inundation above ground level Tuesday and Wednesday, with up to 2.8 ft of inundation expected on Thursday. * WHERE...Beaches and low lying areas along the shore lines of Douglas, Coos and Curry Counties. This includes the communities of North Bend, Charleston, Port Orford, Gold Beach, and Coos Bay. Coastal flooding is expected to impact portions of Highway 101 around Gold Beach, Coos Bay, and Reedsport. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST this afternoon. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 7 AM Tuesday to 7 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. This event is expected see similar impacts to what occurred on January 3rd, 2026. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The worst conditions are expected to be during the high tide periods in the late morning/early afternoon. Storm activity lessens on Thursday, but King Tides will still be present, which will likely continue inundation impacts. At the Charleston, OR tide gauge, high tide is expected to be at 10:09 AM today, at 10:51 AM Tuesday, at 11:35 AM Wednesday, and at 12:23 PM Thursday.

events.title: Coastal Flood Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor to moderate coastal flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to 8 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding expected. For the High Surf Warning, large damaging breaking waves of 8 to 15 feet with dangerous rip currents. * WHERE...Ventura County Beaches. Highest surf along west facing beaches. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 8 AM PST Wednesday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 9 PM Tuesday to 8 AM PST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 8 AM Wednesday to noon PST Thursday. For the High Surf Warning, from 8 AM Wednesday to noon PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Damaging flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beaches (especially from Faria Beach to Silver Strand Beach), roads, and structures. Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers (including Ventura Pier) and jetties. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Large breaking waves may impact Ventura and Channel Islands Harbors. Extremely high tides may cause dock damage and seawater spillage over low lying areas inside of harbor areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Extremely high tides of 8.1-8.5 feet will likely peak between 7am and 11am. Coastal Flood and High Surf Advisories are likely to follow the expiration of the respective warnings.

Largest surf expected on the west side of the islands. * WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until noon PST Thursday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 6 AM Wednesday to 9 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Extremely high tides may cause dock damage and seawater spillage over low lying areas inside of harbor areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Extremely high tides of 8.1-8.4 feet will likely peak between 7am and 11am.

location.region: Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands

events.title: Coastal Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Watch, High astronomical tides and large surf with storm surge may cause moderate flooding in low lying areas along the Redwood/Mendocino Coast. Up to one foot of saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in low lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties. * WHEN...From Tuesday morning through Thursday afternoon during periods of high tide. * IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Expect continued increases in high tide water levels through the coming work week with the tide peaking on Wednesday. Prepare now and pay attention to official guidance on shelters and or resources available to the public.

location.region: Coastal Del Norte; Southwestern Humboldt; Coastal Mendocino

Astronomical Tide or HAT.

events.description: * WHAT...Dangerous rip currents. * WHERE...East facing reefs of the Marianas. * WHEN...Through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A trade-wind swell will continue to produce a high risk of rip currents along east-facing reefs. Surf along east-facing reefs will also be elevated with the rip current risk along north-facing reefs also elevated.

location.region: Guam; Rota; Tinian; Saipan

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 24 at 4:42AM ChST until November 26 at 3:00PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
weather.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...East facing reefs of the Marianas.

* WHEN...Through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A trade-wind swell will continue to produce
a high risk of rip currents along east-facing reefs. Surf along
east-facing reefs will also be elevated with the rip current

weather.instruction:

current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

events.title: Coastal Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding expected. Inundation of 2.5 to 3.5 feet above ground level is possible Tuesday along shorelines and low- lying coastal areas. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves along the coast. For the first Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible Wednesday with inundation up to 2.5 to 3.5 feet. For the second Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible Thursday with inundation up to 2.5 to 3.5 feet. * WHERE...Northern Washington Coast zone. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 8 AM to 3 PM PST Tuesday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 10 AM Tuesday to 4 PM PST Wednesday. For the first Coastal Flood Watch, from late Tuesday night through Wednesday afternoon. For the second Coastal Flood Watch, from late Wednesday night through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Significant coastal flooding due to high tides and storm surge is expected. This is expected to lead to numerous road closures. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure may be inundated. Shoreline erosion or damage may occur. Large breaking waves can knock people off their feet, move driftwood and debris, and crash over rocks and jetties. People can be injured or drown while observing the ocean. Localized beach and coastal erosion is expected.

location.region: Northern Washington Coast

For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 4 AM Tuesday to 1 PM PST Friday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 1 PM Wednesday to 4 AM PST Friday. Surf lowers to 5-7 feet by Friday morning's high tide.

events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible. * WHERE...A portion of northwest Washington, including the following county, Mason. * WHEN...From Wednesday morning through Sunday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - A series of storms will bring roughly 3 to 6 inches of rainfall to the southern slopes of the Olympics through Thursday with snow levels rising to around 5000 to 5500 feet on Tuesday, and as high as 6000 to 6500 feet on Wednesday. The combination of heavy rain and relatively high snow levels is expected to push the Skokomish River near Potlach above flood stage by midweek. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

weather.description:

* WHERE...A portion of northwest Washington, including the following
county, Mason.

* WHEN...From Wednesday morning through Sunday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A series of storms will bring roughly 3 to 6 inches of rainfall
to the southern slopes of the Olympics through Thursday with snow
levels rising to around 5000 to 5500 feet on Tuesday, and as high

and relatively high snow levels is expected to push the Skokomish

to take action should flooding develop.

events.title: Coastal Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Up to 1 to 3 feet of inundation above ground level possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Areas along Bogue Banks beaches, Bogue Sound, the Newport and White Oak Rivers, and adjacent tidal creeks, and areas in North Topsail Beach, the lower New River, and adjacent tidal creeks. * WHEN...From Wednesday evening through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Up to 1 to 3 feet of inundation above ground level is possible in some areas near shorelines and tidal waterways resulting in an elevated threat of property damage. Flooding will extend inland from the waterfront threatening some homes and businesses. Isolated road closures and flooding of vehicles will be possible. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King Tides will be peaking on Wednesday and Thursday before gradually lowering which will continue to bring elevated water levels to the area through much of the week. The King Tides will be exacerbated by a strong coastal low impacting the area Wednesday evening into Thursday morning. The higher of the high tide cycles will be during the morning hours each day this week. This is forecast to bring nuisance water level rises on Tuesday across the watch area with minor to locally moderate impacts forecast on Wednesday. The worst impacts are currently forecast with the morning high tide cycle on Thursday.

Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high tide. * IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. events.description: * WHAT...Higher than normal astronomical tides, the King Tides, combined with storm surge from large surf and breaking wave heights of 23 to 28 ft, are expected to bring up to 3.3 ft of inundation above ground level Tuesday and Wednesday, with up to 2.8 ft of inundation expected on Thursday. * WHERE...Beaches and low lying areas along the shore lines of Douglas, Coos and Curry Counties. Coastal flooding is expected to impact portions of Highway 101 around Gold Beach, Coos Bay, and Reedsport. * WHEN...From 7 AM Tuesday to 7 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The worst conditions are expected to be during the high tide periods in the late morning/early afternoon. Storm activity lessens on Thursday, but King Tides will still be present, which will likely continue inundation impacts. At the Charleston, OR tide gauge, high tide is expected to be at 10:09 AM today, at 10:51 AM Tuesday, at 11:35 AM Wednesday, and at 12:23 PM Thursday.

events.title: Coastal Flood Warning
events.description: * WHAT...Significant coastal flooding with up to 2.7 feet of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...San Francisco and San Pablo Bay Shorelines. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM PST Monday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 6 AM Monday to 4 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, numerous road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide is expected to be 2.4 ft above normal (8.2 ft MLLW) at 10:05 AM Tuesday, 2.7 ft above normal (8.5 ft MLLW) at 10:49 AM Wednesday, and 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents expected.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6 to 8 feet.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding
expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Duval County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 1 AM EST
Wednesday. For the High Rip Current Risk, through late
Wednesday night. For the High Surf Advisory, from 11 PM this
evening to 3 AM EST Thursday. For the Coastal Flood Warning,
from 1 AM to 7 PM EST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

events.title: Coastal Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, High astronomical tides will cause major flooding in low lying areas mainly around Humboldt Bay. Up to 3 of saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in low lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. Between 10.3 and 11.0 feet MLLW at the North Spit tide gauge is predicted. For the Coastal Flood Watch, High astronomical tides and large surf may cause major flooding in low lying areas along the Redwood Coast. Up to 2.5 foot of saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in low lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 9 AM to 1 PM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Wednesday morning through Thursday afternoon. High tide is at 11:09 AM on Wednesday and 11:56 AM on Thursday at the Humboldt Bay North Spit tide gauge. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high tide. * IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. These impacts will include, but not limited to, roadways and houses in King Salmon and the Arcata bottoms. This may also include highway 101 near College of the Redwoods and Hwy 255 near the Mad River Slough. Shoreline erosion will occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The water levels from this are expected to exceed the water levels seen in January of 2026 that caused significant flooding in King Salmon.

For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 4 AM this morning to 1 PM PST Friday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 1 PM Wednesday to 4 AM PST Friday. Background surf on top of the tides will remain around 2-5 feet through Wednesday morning, but a long period west swell arrives Wednesday afternoon, bringing a sharp increase to the surf for late Wednesday into Thursday. Breaking waves may reach 6-8 feet with local sets up to 10 feet on west- facing beaches. Surf lowers to 5-7 feet by Friday morning's high tide.

Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - The last 30 days of rainfall has been 400 to 600 percent of normal across portions of Palm Beach and Broward Counties, and between 200 to 300 percent of normal across portions of Miami-Dade County. This amount of rainfall has made the ground very saturated over the east coast metro areas of South Florida, and thus it will not take much rainfall to create exacerbated flooding issues across the east coast metro areas. Most likely amounts: 2-3 inches of rain Reasonable Worst Case (High-End): 4-6 inches of rain - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents. For the
Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Duval County.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 3 AM EST Thursday.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 1 AM EST Wednesday. For

from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6-8 feet, sets up to 10-12 feet along west-facing beaches. * WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, now through 1 PM PST Friday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 1 PM Wednesday to 4 AM PST Friday. Most susceptible time of flooding will be around the time of the morning high tide, with peak tides trending from 7 AM today to 10 AM on Friday. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King tides peak through Wednesday at 7.9- 8.3 feet, likely breaking the all-time tidal records set back in late October. Background surf on top of the tides will remain around 2-5 feet through Wednesday morning, but a long period west swell arrives Wednesday afternoon, bringing a sharp increase to the surf for late Wednesday into Thursday. Breaking waves may reach 6-8 feet with local sets up to 10 feet on west- facing beaches. Surf lowers to 5-7 feet by Friday morning's high tide.

property.

events.title: Coastal Flood Warning
events.description: * WHAT...Higher than normal astronomical tides, the King Tides, combined with storm surge from large surf and breaking wave heights of 23 to 28 ft, are expected to bring up to 3.3 ft of inundation above ground level today and Wednesday, with up to 2.6 ft of inundation expected on Thursday. * WHERE...Beaches and low lying areas along the shore lines of Douglas, Coos and Curry Counties. This includes the communities of North Bend, Charleston, Port Orford, Gold Beach, and Coos Bay. Coastal flooding is expected to impact portions of Highway 101 around Gold Beach, Coos Bay, and Reedsport. * WHEN...From 7 AM today to 7 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The worst conditions are expected to be during the high tide periods in the late morning/early afternoon. Storm activity lessens on Thursday, but King Tides will still be present, which will likely continue inundation impacts. At the Charleston, OR tide gauge, high tide is expected to be at 11:35 AM Wednesday, at 12:23 PM Thursday, and at 1:14 PM Friday. Tides look to return to more typical heights over the weekend.

weather.description:

waterways.

* WHERE...Inland Sussex and Delaware Beaches.

in coastal and bayside communities, and near inland tidal
waterways. Some locations may become isolated by the flood
waters.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Minor tidal flooding is expected on
Wednesday morning. The most severe and impactful high tide will

weather.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Warning means that moderate or major tidal
flooding is occurring or imminent. Be prepared for rising water
levels and take appropriate action to protect life and property.
Follow the recommendations of local emergency management
officials.

Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The water may be
deeper than you think it is. You will be putting yourself in
danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to costly
repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

flooding may become severe enough to cause structural damage

weather.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Warning means that moderate or major tidal
flooding is occurring or imminent. Be prepared for rising water
levels and take appropriate action to protect life and property.
Follow the recommendations of local emergency management
officials.

Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The water may be
deeper than you think it is. You will be putting yourself in
danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to costly
repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be possible. * WHERE...A portion of southeast Florida, including the following areas, Coastal Broward County, Coastal Miami Dade County, Coastal Palm Beach County, Metro Broward County, Metro Palm Beach County and Metropolitan Miami Dade. * WHEN...From 7 PM EST this evening through late Wednesday night. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. This amount of rainfall has made the ground very saturated over the east coast metro areas of South Florida, and thus it will not take much rainfall to create exacerbated flooding issues across the east coast metro areas. Most likely amounts: 2-3 inches of rain Reasonable Worst Case (High-End): 4-6 inches of rain - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: High Surf Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor to moderate coastal flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 8 to 12 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding expected. For the High Surf Warning, large damaging breaking waves of 15 to 22 feet with dangerous rip currents are expected. * WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM PST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 6 AM Wednesday to noon PST Thursday. For the High Surf Warning, from 6 AM Wednesday to noon PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Damaging flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beaches (especially Oceano Dunes, Pismo Beach, Morro Bay, and Guadalupe Dunes), roads, and structures. Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers (including Cayucos, Avila, and Pismo) and jetties. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Large breaking waves may impact Morro Bay Harbor. Extremely high tides may cause dock damage and seawater spillage over low lying areas inside of harbor areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Extremely high tides of 7.7-8.2 feet will likely peak between 7am and 11am. Coastal Flood and High Surf Advisories are likely to follow the expiration of the respective warnings.

location.region: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches

weather.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 24 at 5:51PM PST until November 26 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor to moderate
coastal flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 8 to 12 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the
Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding expected.
For the High Surf Warning, large damaging breaking waves of 15
to 22 feet with dangerous rip currents are expected.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM PST
Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 6 AM Wednesday
to noon PST Thursday. For the High Surf Warning, from 6 AM
Wednesday to noon PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Damaging flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beaches (especially Oceano Dunes,
Pismo Beach, Morro Bay, and Guadalupe Dunes), roads, and
structures. Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful
waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of
ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers
(including Cayucos, Avila, and Pismo) and jetties. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Large breaking
waves may impact Morro Bay Harbor. Extremely high tides may
cause dock damage and seawater spillage over low lying areas
inside of harbor areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Extremely high tides of 7.7-8.2 feet will
likely peak between 7am and 11am. Coastal Flood and High Surf
Advisories are likely to follow the expiration of the
respective warnings.
weather.instruction:
Stay off of beaches and coastal walkways, roads, and structures.
Do NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other water side
infrastructure.

For the High Surf Warning, large damaging breaking waves of 15 to 22 feet with dangerous rip currents are expected. * WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM PST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 6 AM Wednesday to noon PST Thursday. For the High Surf Warning, from 6 AM Wednesday to noon PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Damaging flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beaches (especially Oceano Dunes, Pismo Beach, Morro Bay, and Guadalupe Dunes), roads, and structures. Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers (including Cayucos, Avila, and Pismo) and jetties. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Large breaking waves may impact Morro Bay Harbor. Extremely high tides may cause dock damage and seawater spillage over low lying areas inside of harbor areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Extremely high tides of 7.7-8.2 feet will likely peak between 7am and 11am. Coastal Flood and High Surf Advisories are likely to follow the expiration of the respective warnings.

These predictions include up to 1.5 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

weather.description:
* WHAT...Up to one foot of inundation above ground level
expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Kent MD.

* WHEN...From 6 PM Thursday to midnight EST Friday night.

weather.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that minor tidal flooding is
expected. Minor tidal flooding often results in some road
closures. Usually, the most vulnerable roadways will flood.

Do not leave your vehicle at a location that is prone to tidal
flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The
water may be deeper than you think it is. You will be putting
yourself in danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to
costly repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

events.title: Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be possible. * WHERE...A portion of southeast Florida, including the following areas, Coastal Broward County, Coastal Miami Dade County, Coastal Palm Beach County, Metro Broward County, Metro Palm Beach County and Metropolitan Miami Dade. * WHEN...Through late tonight. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - The last 30 days of rainfall has been 400 to 600 percent of normal across portions of Palm Beach and Broward Counties, and between 200 to 300 percent of normal across portions of Miami-Dade County. This amount of rainfall has made the ground very saturated over the east coast metro areas of South Florida, and thus it will not take much rainfall to create exacerbated flooding issues across the east coast metro areas. Most likely amounts: 2-4 inches of rain. Reasonable Worst Case (High-End): 5-7 inches of rain. A few locations could see 10 or more inches of rain. - Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents expected. * WHERE...Pinellas, Coastal Hillsborough, Coastal Manatee, Coastal Sarasota, Coastal Charlotte and Coastal Lee Counties. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 8 PM this evening to 5 AM EST Thursday. For the High Rip Current Risk, from late tonight through Thursday evening. * IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only isolated road closures expected. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

location.region: Pinellas; Coastal Hillsborough; Coastal Manatee; Coastal Sarasota; Coastal Charlotte; Coastal Lee

weather.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 25 at 3:01AM EST until November 26 at 5:00AM EST by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding
expected. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip
currents expected.

* WHERE...Pinellas, Coastal Hillsborough, Coastal Manatee,
Coastal Sarasota, Coastal Charlotte and Coastal Lee Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 8 PM this evening
to 5 AM EST Thursday. For the High Rip Current Risk, from late
tonight through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only isolated
road closures expected. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.
weather.areaDesc: Pinellas; Coastal Hillsborough; Coastal Manatee; Coastal Sarasota; Coastal Charlotte; Coastal Lee

weather.headline: High Wind Watch issued November 24 at 11:27PM PST until November 26 at 7:00AM PST by NWS Portland OR
weather.description:
* WHAT...South winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 60 mph possible.

* WHERE...In Oregon, Clatsop County Coast and Tillamook County Coast.
In Washington, South Washington Coast.

* WHEN...From Wednesday evening through Thursday morning.

* IMPACTS...Damaging winds could blow down trees and power lines.
Widespread power outages are possible. Travel could be difficult,
especially for high profile vehicles.
weather.instruction:
Fasten loose objects or shelter objects in a safe location prior to
the onset of winds.

Consider sleeping in a location that is furthest away from large
trees and power lines. Be aware of your surroundings and where you
are relative to nearby trees and powerlines.

Prepare for potential power outages. If you have a gas-powered
generator, ensure you have enough fuel. Ensure you have batteries,
flashlights, and a way to maintain a safe body temperature if you
were to lose heating and cooling.

Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates.

weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5
to 7 feet. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip
currents.

* WHERE...Southeast Georgia Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 7 PM EST this
evening. For the High Surf Advisory, until 3 AM EST Thursday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

events.title: Coastal Flood Warning
events.description: * WHAT...Higher than normal astronomical tides, the King Tides, combined with storm surge from large surf and breaking wave heights of 23 to 28 ft, are expected to bring up to 3.3 ft of inundation above ground level Wednesday, with up to 2.6 ft of inundation expected on Thursday. * WHERE...Beaches and low lying areas along the shore lines of Douglas, Coos and Curry Counties. This includes the communities of North Bend, Charleston, Port Orford, Gold Beach, and Coos Bay. Coastal flooding is expected to impact portions of Highway 101 around Gold Beach, Coos Bay, and Reedsport. * WHEN...Until 7 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The worst conditions are expected to be during the high tide periods in the late morning/early afternoon. Storm activity lessens on Thursday, but King Tides will still be present, which will likely continue inundation impacts. At the Charleston, Oregon tide gauge, high tide is expected to be at 11:35 AM Wednesday, at 12:23 PM Thursday, and at 1:14 PM Friday. Tides look to return to more typical heights over the weekend.

location.region: South Central Oregon Coast; Curry County Coast

weather.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Warning means that flooding is occurring or
imminent. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert
for rising water and take appropriate action to protect life and
property.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.

capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

events.title: Coastal Flood Warning
events.description: * WHAT...Significant coastal flooding expected. * WHERE...Orange County Coastal Areas. * WHEN...Through 1 PM PST Friday. Most susceptible time of flooding will be around the time of the morning high tide, with peak tides trending from 8 AM today to 10 AM on Friday. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King tides peak each day through Thursday at 7.9-8.3 feet, likely breaking the all-time tidal records set back in late October. A long period west swell arrives late this afternoon and will bring elevated to high surf by Thursday morning's high tide. Breaking waves may reach 4-6 feet with local sets up to 7-8 feet on west-facing beaches. Surf lowers to 3-5 feet by Friday morning's high tide.

The forecast has been leaned towards a higher end water level scenario to provide a bit of safety margin. If the timing of strongest winds is quicker than currently forecast the peak water level forecast could be increased by a few tenths for Thursday morning. if slower the Thursday morning forecast could be lowered slightly.

For the St. Johns River...including Above Lake Harney...Major
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
The river crest has surpassed its previous flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 10.8 feet, Water covers State Road 46 and it may
become impassable near Jungle Road and Prevatt Road. Standing water
on secondary roads near the river deepens to more than three feet
in some areas. Flooding becomes more significant to structures and
marinas from above Lake Harney to the Lake Jesup area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:30 PM EST Wednesday the stage was 13.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 1:30 PM EST Wednesday was 13.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 13.3 feet
this evening.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Thursday morning at 1100 AM EST.

Inundation of 2.5 to 3.5 feet above ground level is possible Thursday along shorelines and low-lying coastal areas. * WHERE...San Juan County zone. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST this afternoon. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 3 AM to 10 AM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Significant coastal flooding due to high tides and storm surge is expected. This is expected to lead to numerous road closures. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure may be inundated. Shoreline erosion or damage may occur.

weather.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 25 at 9:39AM PST until November 26 at 10:00AM PST by NWS Seattle WA
weather.description:

expected. Inundation of 1 to 2 feet above ground level is
possible this afternoon along shorelines and low- lying coastal
areas. For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding expected. Inundation of 2.5 to 3.5 feet above ground
level is possible Thursday along shorelines and low-lying
coastal areas.

* WHERE...San Juan County zone.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST this
afternoon. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 3 AM to 10 AM
PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Significant coastal flooding due to high tides and
storm surge is expected. This is expected to lead to numerous
road closures. Low lying property including homes, businesses,
and some critical infrastructure may be inundated. Shoreline
erosion or damage may occur.
weather.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inundation above ground level refers to the height above the Mean
Higher High Water (MHHW) level.

weather.description:
...The National Weather Service in Seattle has issued a Flood Warning
for the following rivers in Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

.Heavy rain over the Olypics overnight plus an additional 2-4 inches
of rain, with snow levels well above mountain tops will drive the
Skokomish River above flood stage this afternoon to above Moderate
flood.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast. This approaches the flood of
record.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...From this afternoon to Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 17.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause moderate
flooding, with deep and quick flood waters inundating some
residential areas, many roads, and much of the farm land in the
Skokomish Valley. Inundated roads include the Skokomish Valley
road, Bourgault Road West, Purdy Cutoff Road, and Highway 106.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM PST Wednesday the stage was 15.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise above flood stage this afternoon
to 17.9 feet late tonight. It will then fall below flood stage
late Friday morning. Further rises through the weekend are
likely, with exceeding flood stage possible.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this afternoon at 530 PM PST.

events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding expected. For the High Surf Warning, large damaging breaking waves of 15 to 22 feet with dangerous rip currents are expected. * WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches. * WHEN...Until noon PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Damaging flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beaches (especially Oceano Dunes, Pismo Beach, Morro Bay, and Guadalupe Dunes), roads, and structures. Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers (including Cayucos, Avila, and Pismo) and jetties. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Large breaking waves may impact Morro Bay Harbor. Extremely high tides may cause dock damage and seawater spillage over low lying areas inside of harbor areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Extremely high tides of around 7.8 feet will likely peak between 8 AM and 11 AM. Coastal Flood and High Surf Advisories are likely to follow the expiration of the respective warnings.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor to moderate coastal flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6 to 11 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible. * WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM PST Thursday. For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Thursday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, Thursday morning. * IMPACTS...There is a moderate risk for damaging flooding of sea water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beaches (especially from Santa Monica to Palos Verdes and Malibu), roads, and structures. Significant beach erosion is possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Extremely high tides may cause dock damage and seawater spillage over low lying areas inside of harbor areas (such as Naples in Long Beach). * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Extremely high tides of 8.0-8.2 feet will likely peak between 8 AM and 11 AM. An upgrade to a Coastal Flood Warning would likely come by late today. Coastal Flood and High Surf Advisories are likely to follow the expiration of the respective warnings if they are issued.

events.title: High Surf Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding expected. For the High Surf Warning, large damaging breaking waves of 15 to 22 feet with dangerous rip currents are expected. * WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches. * WHEN...Until noon PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Damaging flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beaches (especially Oceano Dunes, Pismo Beach, Morro Bay, and Guadalupe Dunes), roads, and structures. Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers (including Cayucos, Avila, and Pismo) and jetties. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Large breaking waves may impact Morro Bay Harbor. Extremely high tides may cause dock damage and seawater spillage over low lying areas inside of harbor areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Extremely high tides of around 7.8 feet will likely peak between 8 AM and 11 AM. Coastal Flood and High Surf Advisories are likely to follow the expiration of the respective warnings.

breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Extremely high
tides may cause dock damage and seawater spillage over low
lying areas inside of harbor areas (such as Naples in Long
Beach).

likely peak between 8 AM and 11 AM. An upgrade to a Coastal

High Surf Advisories are likely to follow the expiration of the
respective warnings if they are issued.
weather.instruction:

for extra travel time as some roads may be closed.

such conditions, stay off the rocks.

events.title: Coastal Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, High astronomical tides will cause major flooding in low lying areas mainly around Humboldt Bay. Up to 2 feet of saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in low lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. Between 10.0 and 10.4 feet above MLLW at the North Spit tide gauge is predicted. For the Coastal Flood Watch, High astronomical tides and large surf may cause major flooding in low lying areas along the Redwood Coast. Up to 2.5 foot of saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in low lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves up to 25 feet. Surf may worsen coastal flooding along exposed beaches. * WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 9 AM to 1 PM PST Wednesday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 7 AM to 7 PM PST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Thursday morning through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. These impacts will include, but not limited to, roadways in King Salmon and the Arcata bottoms and sections of Highway 101. Shoreline erosion will occur. Dangerous surf conditions and localized beach erosion. Beachcombing is highly discouraged!. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The water levels from this are expected to rival the water levels seen in January of 2026 that caused significant flooding in King Salmon.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint

* IMPACTS...Some flooding of low-lying lots, parks and roadways

weather.instruction:
Onshore winds and above normal tides will combine to generate
flooding of low areas along the shore. Do not drive around
barricades or through water of unknown depth. Take the necessary
actions to protect flood-prone property.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

weather.headline: High Wind Warning issued November 25 at 12:28PM PST until November 26 at 7:00AM PST by NWS Portland OR
weather.description:
* WHAT...South winds 25 to 35 mph with gusts up to 60 mph expected
for beaches and headlands.

* WHERE...Central Coast of Oregon.

* WHEN...From 10 PM this evening to 7 AM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Damaging winds will blow down trees and power lines. Some
power outages are expected. Travel will be difficult for high
profile vehicles.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The period of strongest winds are expected to
occur between 3-7 AM PST Thursday. Although it will be windy for
inland coastal communities, maximum gusts will be relatively weaker
compared to beaches and headlands with gusts up to 50-55 mph.
weather.instruction:
A High Wind Warning for the coastal headlands and beaches means a
hazardous high wind event is expected or occurring in those areas
along the immediate coast. Many of the headland areas and beaches are
vulnerable to very strong wind gusts that may pose a safety hazard
for individuals or high profile vehicles. The strong winds may also
cause property and/or tree damage. Sustained wind speeds of at least
40 mph or gusts of 58 mph or more are expected in those areas.
Coastal headlands are characterized by high, rocky shores and steep
sea cliffs.

Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.
weather.areaDesc: Central Coast of Oregon

events.title: Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be possible. * WHERE...A portion of southeast Florida, including the following areas, Coastal Broward County, Coastal Miami Dade County, Coastal Palm Beach County, Metro Broward County, Metro Palm Beach County and Metropolitan Miami Dade. * WHEN...Until 1 AM EST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - The last 30 days of rainfall has been 400 to 600 percent of normal across portions of Palm Beach and Broward Counties, and between 200 to 300 percent of normal across portions of Miami-Dade County. This amount of rainfall has made the ground very saturated over the east coast metro areas of South Florida, and thus it will not take much rainfall to create exacerbated flooding issues across the east coast metro areas. Most likely amounts: 2-4 inches of rain. Reasonable Worst Case (High-End): 5-7 inches of rain. A few locations could see 10 or more inches of rain. - Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: Coastal Flood Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 8 to 12 feet expected in the surf zone. For the Coastal Flood Warning, 2 to 4 feet of inundation above ground level expected in low- lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Northern Outer Banks. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 10 AM EST Friday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 7 PM this evening to 3 PM EST Friday. * IMPACTS...Up to 2 to 4 feet of inundation above ground level is possible in low lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways resulting in a elevated threat of property damage. Flooding will extend inland from the waterfront threatening some homes and businesses. Isolated road closures and flooding of vehicles will be possible. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Greatest impacts expected Thursday morning. As winds switch to a SW direction Thursday afternoon, minor water level rises (around 1-2 ft) on soundside locations will be possible.

deeper than you think it is. You will be putting yourself in
danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to costly
repairs.

weather.instruction:

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

A High Surf Advisory means that high surf will affect beaches in
the advisory area, producing localized beach erosion and
dangerous swimming conditions.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...High astronomical tides will cause minor flooding in low lying areas around Humboldt Bay. Up to 1 foot of saltwater inundation above ground level is possible near shorelines and tidal waterways. Between 9.5 and 9.8 feet MLLW at the North Spit tide gauge is predicted. * WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Northern Coastal Humboldt, Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties. * WHEN...From 8 AM to 3 PM PST Thursday. High tide is at 12:54 PM at the Humboldt Bay North Spit tide gauge. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high tide. * IMPACTS...Flooding of low lying areas around Humboldt Bay including parks and roads with only isolated closures expected. Flooding will likely impact Jackson Ranch Road in the Arcata Bottoms and several roads in King Salmon. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The water levels from this event will be higher than normal but not quite as high as the previous near record recording from Tuesday 11/24 at 10.16 feet.

location.region: Coastal Del Norte; Northern Coastal Humboldt; Southwestern Humboldt; Coastal Mendocino

weather.description:
* WHAT...High astronomical tides will cause minor flooding in low
lying areas around Humboldt Bay. Up to 1 foot of saltwater
inundation above ground level is possible near shorelines and
tidal waterways. Between 9.5 and 9.8 feet MLLW at the North Spit
tide gauge is predicted.

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Northern Coastal Humboldt,
Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...From 8 AM to 3 PM PST Thursday. High tide is at 12:54 PM
at the Humboldt Bay North Spit tide gauge. Saltwater inundation

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low lying areas around Humboldt Bay
including parks and roads with only isolated closures

higher than normal but not quite as high as the previous near
record recording from Tuesday 11/24 at 10.16 feet.
weather.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory indicates that onshore winds and tides
will combine to generate flooding of low areas along the shore.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, 1 1/2 to 2 1/2 ft of inundation above ground level expected in vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, 1 to 1 1/2 ft of inundation above ground level possible in vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline. * WHERE...Northeast Suffolk County. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 7 AM Thursday to 6 AM EST Friday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 8 AM to 4 PM EST Friday. * COASTAL FLOOD IMPACTS...Widespread moderate flooding of vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline, including roads, parking lots, parks, lawns, and homes and businesses with basements near the waterfront. Numerous road closures are likely, and vehicles parked in vulnerable areas near the waterfront will likely become flooded. Flooding will also extend inland from the waterfront along tidal rivers and bays. * SHORELINE IMPACTS...Breaking waves of 4 to 8 ft will result in areas of dune erosion and localized overwashes. Wave splashover will exacerbate flooding of roadways and vulnerable structures behind protective dunes and seawalls. There is potential for isolated damage to shoreline and marina structures as well. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The highest water levels are likely with the Thursday morning and evening high tides. The forecast has been leaned towards a higher end water level scenario to provide a bit of safety margin. If the timing of strongest winds is quicker than currently forecast the peak water level forecast could be increased by a few tenths for Thursday morning, and if slower the Thursday morning forecast could be lowered slightly. Similarly if strongest winds linger later into the evening, the Thursday evening water level forecast could be a few tenths higher.

For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking waves of 20 to 30 feet. * WHERE...Pacific Coast. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory through 4 PM PST Thursday. For the High Surf Warning, through midnight PST Wednesday night. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, numerous road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of drowning. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide is expected to be 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

weather.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow. Additional snow accumulations between 4 and 7
inches.

* WHERE...Franklin MO, Warren MO, and Pike MO Counties.

* WHEN...Until noon CST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions

weather.instruction:
The rapid accumulation of snow will make travel extremely difficult,
if not impossible. If travel is necessary, be sure to exercise
extreme caution. If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food
and water in your vehicle in case of an emergency. In Illinois, the
latest road conditions can be obtained at

conditions can be obtained at traveler.modot.org/map or by calling
1-888-275-6636.

weather.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow. Additional snow accumulations between 5 and 12
inches.

* WHERE...Crawford MO, Reynolds MO, Saint Francois MO, and Sainte
Genevieve MO Counties.

* WHEN...Until 6 PM CST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Roads, and especially bridges and overpasses, will likely
become slick and hazardous. The strong winds and weight of snow on
tree limbs may down power lines and could cause sporadic power
outages.
weather.instruction:
Persons should delay all travel if possible. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution and be prepared for sudden
changes in visibility. Leave plenty of room between you and the
motorist ahead of you, and allow extra time to reach your
destination. Avoid sudden braking or acceleration, and be especially
cautious on hills or when making turns. Make sure your car is
winterized and in good working order.

weather.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 25 at 7:03PM EST until November 26 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Jacksonville FL
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6 to 9 feet.
For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Duval, Coastal Flagler, Northeast Coastal St.
Johns and Southeast Coastal St. Johns Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 7 PM EST
Thursday. For the High Surf Advisory, until 4 AM EST Thursday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, until 4 AM EST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Dangerous swimming and
surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents
can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper
water.
weather.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.
weather.areaDesc: Coastal Duval; Coastal Flagler; Northeast Coastal St. Johns; Southeast Coastal St. Johns

weather.description: The Coastal Flood Watch has been replaced. Please see the latest information from NWS Eureka CA on this developing situation.
weather.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory indicates that onshore winds and tides
will combine to generate flooding of low areas along the shore.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

Inundated roads include the Skokomish Valley road, Bourgault Road West, Purdy Cutoff Road, and Highway 106. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 1:30 PM PST Wednesday the stage was 16.6 feet. - Forecast...The river will rise to 17.9 feet late tomorrow morning. ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in

.Heavy rain over the Olympics overnight plus an additional 2-4 inches
of rain, with snow levels well above mountain tops, will drive the
Skokomish River above flood stage this evening to above Moderate
flood.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast. This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...Until Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 17.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause moderate
flooding, with deep and quick flood waters inundating some
residential areas, many roads, and much of the farm land in the
Skokomish Valley. Inundated roads include the Skokomish Valley
road, Bourgault Road West, Purdy Cutoff Road, and Highway 106.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:30 PM PST Wednesday the stage was 16.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise to 17.9 feet late tomorrow
morning. It will then fall below flood stage late Friday morning.
Further rises through the weekend are likely, with exceeding
flood stage possible.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1030 PM PST.

For the Coastal Flood Warning, until noon PST Thursday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 3 AM Thursday to noon PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...Damaging flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beaches (especially Oceano Dunes, Pismo Beach, Morro Bay, and Guadalupe Dunes), roads, and structures. Extremely high tides may cause dock damage and seawater spillage over low lying areas inside of harbor areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...An extreme high tide of 7.8 feet will peak between 9 AM and 11 AM Thursday morning.

Most susceptible time of flooding will be around the time of the morning high tide, around 9 AM on Thursday and 10 PM on Friday. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King tides on Thursday will be around 8 feet. Background surf on top of the tides will remain around 3-6 feet today. A long period west swell arrives late this afternoon and will bring elevated to high surf by Thursday morning's high tide.
